base_properties.human_readable: Magisterial Authority over AI Governance (Imago Dei Integralist Reading)

omegas.question: This constraint is one reading (magisterial_integralist_reading) of the human_dignity_ai_governance kernel; what would each sibling reading change structurally, and where exactly is the disagreement located?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative classification across the four sibling stories: differences in victim sets, authority loci, and epsilon locate the disagreement structurally rather than rhetorically.
omegas.impact: Sibling readings instantiate different constraints: the secular humanist reading relocates authority to democratic deliberation and shifts the victim set to include religious imposition; the techno-optimist reading inverts the victim set (restriction itself becomes the harm); the pluralist reading dissolves the unique-authority claim entirely. This story's classification must not be averaged across them.
omegas.description: Committer structure: one reading of a four-reading kernel; disagreement located in dignity's source and governance authority's locus.

omegas.question: Is the imago Dei dignity premise a mind-independent feature of the moral order (as the reading claims), or a constructed constraint maintained by institutional enforcement?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Metaethical analysis plus cross-cultural convergence testing: convergence of dignity constraints across unrelated traditions without transmission supports natural-law status; divergence tracking to institutional propagation supports construction.
omegas.impact: If constructed, the constraint's full profile runs tangled_rope toward snare and the false-summit signature applies; if genuinely natural law, part of the measured extraction is the price of conforming to reality rather than extractive overhead.
omegas.description: Naturality ambiguity of the dignity premise (false-summit documentation carried even under a non-mountain claim).

omegas.question: How much of the constraint's operation rests on genuinely voluntary adoption versus structural dependency of people inside Catholic institutional networks (employees, patients, students) who cannot cheaply opt out?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Exit-cost surveys and mobility data for populations employed and served by Catholic institutions; comparison of conformity rates between captive and non-captive audiences.
omegas.impact: Higher dependency means effective extraction on internal populations exceeds the voluntary-adoption framing; the payer computation for internal members shifts toward the trapped-target end and the seat divergence widens.
omegas.description: Voluntariness depth of adoption inside the institutional sphere.

omegas.question: Does the measured suppression operate mainly inside the Catholic institutional sphere (where enforcement is strong) or across society at large (where the Church holds little coercive power)? The single scalar blends both regimes.
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Stratified measurement by jurisdiction and institutional context: enforcement incidents, employment consequences, and conscience-appeal outcomes inside versus outside the network.
omegas.impact: Inside-sphere dominance supports high suppression for internal seats and near-zero for external ones, widening seat divergence; a uniform reading would misclassify one population or the other.
omegas.description: Bimodal suppression profile across the sphere boundary.

omegas.question: Is the Magisterium's claimed unique competence an expertise claim assessable by results, or a lineage claim grounded in divine institution and therefore not empirically falsifiable?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Analysis of the claim's self-understanding in magisterial documents: whether the Church offers success criteria for its guidance or grounds authority in apostolic succession irrespective of outcomes.
omegas.impact: If expertise-framed, documented failures in applied guidance would erode the constraint's authority and eventually its enforcement capacity; if lineage-framed, the constraint is drift-resistant and decay comes only through institutional attrition.
omegas.description: Epistemic type of the unique-authority claim.

commentary.narrative_context: A governance arrangement in which AI development is held to conformity with Catholic Social Doctrine as interpreted by the Magisterium, grounded in the claim that human dignity is an ontological gift from God (imago Dei) — infinite, inalienable, knowable through faith and reason — and that the Church possesses unique authority to guide technological development toward the common good. Operationally the arrangement runs through doctrinal instruments addressed to the AI sector, uptake across a global network of Catholic hospitals, universities, schools, and charities, multi-religious and industry convening, and enforcement by moral suasion, institutional discipline, and appeal to conscience. KEY AGENTS (by structural relationship): - magisterium_holy_see: Agenda setter (institutional/identity_locked) — issues binding interpretation, collects authority; - catholic_institutional_network: Administering beneficiary (organized/identity_locked) — enforces locally, receives guidance and legitimacy; - automation_displaced_workers: Protected beneficiary (moderate/constrained); - elderly_and_disabled_persons: Paradigm-protected beneficiary (powerless/trapped); - family_households: Protected beneficiary (moderate/constrained); - secular_ai_developers: Nominal payer with arbitrage-grade exit (powerful/arbitrage); - transhumanist_research_programs: Ideological payer (moderate/constrained); - technocratic_policy_elites: Legitimacy-contested payer (institutional/mobile); - dissenting_catholic_technologists: Internal payer (moderate/identity_locked); - non_christian_dignity_traditions: Excluded rival authorities (organized/trapped-out); - comparative_ai_ethics_observers: Analytical observer. Per the epsilon-invariance principle this story decomposes the colloquial label 'human dignity in AI governance' into four structurally distinct constraints — one per sibling reading — linked via network.affects_constraints. This file authors epsilon for the standing magisterial-conformity arrangement itself, as the integralist reading assesses it (moderate: real costs conceded, judged justified) — never for the secular status quo the reading criticizes and never for the fully integrated Catholic order it endorses. The claimed type and the metrics are independent authored facts.
commentary.logic_rationale: Epsilon is authored at 0.52 — moderate — because the reading's own lights concede real, identifiable costs: design-level conformity to Catholic anthropology, foreclosed enhancement programs, subordinated secular expert judgment, and conscience pressure on dissenting members, while enforcement remains suasion-based and formally voluntary. Suppression (0.48) is authored as raw structure and is NOT scaled by power or scope — only extractiveness is scaled by directionality and scope in the engine's computation; the suppression profile is bimodal, strong inside Catholic institutions (employment, standing, sacramental community) and weak outside them. Theater (0.25) reflects a growing layer of documents, symposia, and signatures outrunning design-level uptake. Accessibility_collapse (0.40): alternatives remain fully available outside the sphere and collapse almost completely inside it — a Catholic hospital cannot adopt utilitarian triage without ceasing to be Catholic. Resistance (0.50): open defiance by transhumanist and technocratic seats, quiet internal dissent, compliance within the fold. The three measurement series share one grid (t = 0,3,6,9,12,15, mapping approximately 2010–2025); suppression_requirement is tracked because the story's dynamic is enforcement-capacity buildout — from general moral teaching to an AI-specific apparatus (Rome Call 2020, Dignitas Infinita 2024, Antiqua et Nova 2025) — not merely shifting extraction. Coalition check: the payer seats are ideologically disjoint (transhumanists, secular technocrats, and faithful dissenters share no framework), so coalition power against the arrangement is improbable despite their combined weight. Claim and metrics are independent: tangled_rope is asserted from structure (genuine coordination function + asymmetric extraction + active enforcement); the metrics describe operation as observed.
commentary.perspectival_gap: The seats compute differently from the same structure. From the Magisterium's seat the arrangement is custodial: persons are threatened by reductionist optimization and the Church supplies the missing defense. From the transhumanist and dissenting-Catholic seats the same structure is illegitimate authority — blocking flourishing in one case, policing conscience in the other. From the secular developer's seat it is a boundary compliance cost routed around at will. From the protected beneficiary seats (workers, elderly, families) it is advocacy and standing they could not generate alone. The engine computes these divergent per-seat classifications from power, exit, and role data; the divergence, not any single verdict, is the finding.
commentary.directionality_logic: Beneficiary declarations drive low d: automation-displaced workers, elderly and disabled persons, family households, and the Catholic institutional network are subsidized by the arrangement (advocacy, protection, coherent standards). The Magisterium sits nearest the beneficiary pole — it collects the arrangement's principal gains (interpretive authority, agenda-setting power) — and is authored as agenda_setter with secondary_role beneficiary so the structural derivation reads its collection rather than falling back to a canonical default. Victim declarations drive high d: transhumanist programs (constrained exit, ideologically unable to adopt without dissolving their purpose), technocratic policy elites (legitimacy costs, damped by mobile exit), and dissenting Catholic technologists (highest effective extraction — identity_locked exit amplifies toward the full-target end). Secular developers hold the payer role but arbitrage-grade exit damps their effective extraction hard. Trapped beneficiaries (elderly, disabled) anchor the subsidy end. Suppression is not scaled; extractiveness is.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The classification guards both directions. Against the snare mislabel: the coordination function is genuine and independently valuable — a global institutional network gets a workable shared standard, and vulnerable groups receive advocacy they cannot self-supply — so a pure-extraction reading fails the coordination requirement. Against the rope mislabel: extraction is real and asymmetric — identifiable parties bear costs they did not consent to and cannot shed inside the sphere — so a pure-coordination reading fails the asymmetry test. Mandatrophy: the founding problem (reduction of persons to measurable inputs) is live and intensifying; founding_problem_status=live paired with disappearance_verdict=world_rearranges yields no mismatch flag, and the constraint is no piton candidate — the administrator actively maintains and extends the arrangement because it collects authority from doing so, and the identity-lock dynamics mean internal payers mostly accommodate rather than exit. If the Catholic identity frame broke (for example, a schism over AI ethics), internal extraction would convert to open exit and the suppression profile would drop sharply.
commentary.kernel_context: Kernel: human_dignity_ai_governance — the contested question of what human dignity is and who may govern AI in its name. This file instantiates the magisterial_integralist_reading: dignity as ontological divine gift (imago Dei), infinite and inalienable, knowable through faith and reason; AI governance bound by Catholic Social Doctrine under Magisterial interpretation; the Church as unique authorized guide toward the common good. Sibling readings — secular_humanist (rational-autonomy grounding, democratic deliberation), techno_optimist (dignity through augmentation, minimal restriction), pluralist_pragmatic (negotiated overlap, no privileged foundation) — are separate constraints, not averaged here. The disagreement is located in dignity's source and in the locus of governance authority. Reading_relations are uniformly forecloses because this is an exclusive-foundation kernel: unlike justification-plural kernels (e.g., capital punishment, where rival justifications of a shared practice coexist), each reading's core premise is the negation of the others' — no single commitment framework can hold 'the Magisterium uniquely authorizes' together with 'no religious authority governs,' 'no foundation is privileged,' or 'dignity is produced by augmentation.' The uniform distribution is warranted by the kernel's structure, not defaulted.

network.dual_formulation_note: Constraint-family decomposition of the human_dignity_ai_governance kernel per the epsilon-invariance principle: the colloquial label 'human dignity in AI governance' covers four structurally distinct claims differing in dignity's source (divine gift / rational autonomy / contested construct / capability product) and in governance authority's locus (Magisterium / democratic deliberation / negotiated consensus / market-individual choice). Each reading is a separate story with its own epsilon, beneficiary/victim structure, and classification; this story authors epsilon for the magisterial-conformity arrangement as the integralist reading assesses it (moderate: real conformity costs conceded, judged justified). The upstream labor-ethics constraint (Rerum Novarum lineage) supplies the doctrinal machinery this reading deploys on the AI domain; sibling readings are linked as family members, never averaged into this classification.

stakeholders.name: magisterium_holy_see
stakeholders.situation: Issues binding interpretations of what AI governance requires — declaring dignity infinite and inalienable in documents addressed to the AI sector, convening multi-religious and industry signatories, and adjudicating disputed applications through its dicasteries. Collects interpretive authority, institutional relevance, and agenda-setting power from the arrangement. Cannot abandon the claim without dissolving the teaching office's own warrant; exit from the arrangement is identical to exit from its identity.

stakeholders.name: catholic_institutional_network
stakeholders.situation: Hospitals, universities, schools, and charities that administer the standard locally: ethics committees screen clinical algorithms, procurement rules require anthropological conformity, curricula teach the doctrine. Receives coherent guidance, moral legitimacy, and differentiation in care and education markets. Bears compliance costs and polices dissent among staff; a member institution that adopted secular utilitarian frameworks would forfeit its Catholic identity and standing.

stakeholders.name: automation_displaced_workers
stakeholders.situation: Workers whose livelihoods are threatened by algorithmic management and automation. The doctrine's labor teachings give their claims standing against pure-efficiency deployment decisions and supply institutional allies — labor chaplains, Catholic union traditions, shareholder activism. Protection depends on employers voluntarily adopting the standard; where no Catholic leverage exists, the benefit is rhetorical.

stakeholders.name: elderly_and_disabled_persons
stakeholders.situation: Care recipients in hospitals and long-term care where AI triage, monitoring, and companion systems are deployed. The doctrine insists care technology must preserve relational presence and never substitute optimization for human contact. They benefit when institutions comply and cannot exit the care regimes the standards govern; they are the paradigm case invoked to justify the arrangement.

stakeholders.name: family_households
stakeholders.situation: Households navigating attention-extractive platforms, data-harvesting nursery technology, and screens displacing parental formation. The doctrine supplies normative backing for resisting these deployments and frames the family as the first society entitled to protection. The backing is advisory; platform economics continue regardless.

stakeholders.name: secular_ai_developers
stakeholders.situation: Commercial labs and platform companies that encounter the constraint mainly at the boundary — when selling into Catholic health systems, joining multi-stakeholder ethics initiatives, or responding to episcopal statements. Conformity requests are treated as market-access costs or public-relations items; the core business proceeds untouched, and routing around the constraint is cheap.

stakeholders.name: transhumanist_research_programs
stakeholders.situation: Movements and laboratories pursuing radical life extension, cognitive enhancement, and substrate independence. The doctrine condemns their core projects as violations of created nature and treats finitude as constitutive of persons rather than a defect to repair. Wherever Catholic institutional weight reaches — bioethics councils, funding partners, public discourse — they lose legitimacy and access; they cannot adopt the standard without dissolving their purpose, so within influenced spaces their option set is resist or marginalize.

stakeholders.name: technocratic_policy_elites
stakeholders.situation: Regulators, standards-body professionals, and governance experts building AI policy through secular and multistakeholder channels. The constraint contests their epistemic monopoly by asserting a non-elected religious authority with unique competence. They bear legitimacy costs — either sharing governance space with a claimant they regard as pre-modern, or dismissing it and absorbing criticism for exclusion. Mobile exit: they operate comfortably in jurisdictions and forums where the claim carries no weight.

stakeholders.name: dissenting_catholic_technologists
stakeholders.situation: Engineers, researchers, and bioethicists formed in the tradition who work in AI and dispute particular applications — the treatment of enhancement, brain-computer interfaces, or the adequacy of magisterial technical competence. They face conscience pressure, professional-standing risk inside Catholic institutions, and the charge of dissent. Exit means leaving the community that constitutes much of their identity, so most accommodate quietly while bearing the cost.

stakeholders.name: non_christian_dignity_traditions
stakeholders.situation: Islamic, Jewish, Buddhist, Hindu, and other traditions with their own developed dignity frameworks and AI ethics. The uniqueness claim positions them as lacking authoritative guidance and invites them as signatories rather than co-authors — present at convened events but outside the interpretive chair. They would object to proxy governance of their communities' technology ethics; they stand outside the conversation the arrangement structures.

stakeholders.name: comparative_ai_ethics_observers
stakeholders.situation: Academic scholars of religion-and-technology, bioethics, and governance who study the arrangement's operation — its uptake in institutions, its enforcement patterns, its effects on design practice — without collecting from it or bearing its costs.

six_questions.coordination_function: Provides a single authoritative anthropological standard — the person as relational, embodied, finite yet transcendent — by which a global network of institutions evaluates AI systems, replacing per-institution improvisation with shared criteria: relational presence in care, priority of labor over capital efficiency, subsidiarity in design governance, family integrity against attention extraction.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves interpretive authority and moral legitimacy from secular technocracy and commercial developers to the Magisterium and compliant institutions; moves conformity costs (design constraints, foreclosed research programs, subordinated expert judgment) onto developers, policy elites, and dissenting members; moves protective standing and advocacy resources toward workers, the elderly and disabled, and families.
six_questions.absent_voices: Non-Christian dignity traditions are invited as signatories but seated outside the interpretive chair the uniqueness claim reserves; secular liberal ethicists and transhumanist advocates have no seat — their positions are adjudicated rather than negotiated; care recipients themselves rarely enter the discernment processes conducted on their behalf. Unanimity within the arrangement partly reflects these absences.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: Catholic health and education networks would lose their shared screening standard and fragment into ad hoc procurement; vulnerable-population advocacy would lose its largest institutional ally; the multi-religious AI-ethics coalition the Vatican convenes would dissolve; and the Church's voice in technology policy would vanish — the governance conversation would rearrange around secular and multistakeholder bodies alone.
six_questions.founding_problem: Industrial and now algorithmic systems that reduce persons to measurable inputs — the tradition was forged from Rerum Novarum onward against factory capitalism's treatment of workers as labor units, and is now extended against AI's treatment of persons as data points, optimization targets, and replaceable presences.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: The problem is corroborated from outside the benefiting parties: secular algorithmic-management research, ILO and OECD reporting on automation displacement, elder-care technology critiques in the gerontology literature, and platform-accountability scholarship all independently document the reduction-of-persons problem. What no external source corroborates is the proposed remedy — magisterial interpretive authority — which is attested only by the Church herself; the problem is externally corroborated, the cure is not.
